Federal taxable income = 315,750.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 300,000.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, single. Line 9 federal AGI 315,750.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions 0.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 15,750.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 0.00: federal AGI 315,750.00 is over the worksheet's printed ceiling 36,667.00 for this status, so the worksheet is not completed. Line 15 PIT-ADJ deductions and exemptions 0.00. Line 17 = 315,750.00 + 0.00 - 15,750.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 300,000.00. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income 300,000.00 = 300,000.00; less base deductions 0.00 gives 300,000.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 5,500.00 = 82.5 + 3.2% x 11,000.00 = 352 + 4.3% x 17,000.00 = 731 + 4.7% x 33,000.00 = 1,551 + 4.9% x 143,500.00 = 7,031.5 + 5.9% x 90,000.00 = 5,310; total 15,058, to the cent 15,058.00. The printed section on T-7 gives 15,056.00; expected keeps the schedule figure 15,058.00, 2.00 more. Lines 19 to 21 0.00. Line 22 net New Mexico income tax 15,058.00.
accepted_approximations: Over 100,000 the printed section is base plus rate, and each base is the table's last row (midpoint 99,950), not the tax at 100,000. A bracket schedule cannot hold that step down, so the schedule gives more than the printed section at every income over 100,000.
